\paragraph{Hypothesized mechanism: embedding similarity as a confusability proxy.}
\looseness=-1
We hypothesize that the predictive power of SCS rests on partial alignment between pretrained embedding spaces and LLM type representations. Both sentence encoders and autoregressive LLMs internalize distributional regularities from overlapping pretraining corpora, so types that are near neighbors in embedding space tend to occupy adjacent regions in the LLM's representation space. When the prompt schema forces discrimination among semantically close types, the model faces an interference effect: high-similarity competitors activate overlapping representations, increasing substitution errors---a pattern consistent with the ecological confusability framework of \citet{baan-2023-ecological}. The remaining ${\sim}$73\% of FewRel batch-level accuracy variance likely reflects prompt formatting, type definition quality, sentence complexity, and mention ambiguity; direct confirmation via attention or representation analysis remains future work.

\looseness=-1
This explains the NER--RE batch-level asymmetry: NER errors concentrate in span boundary and missed-entity modes (Figure~\ref{fig:error_taxonomy}), so BCS---which captures type-confusion potential---lacks batch-level predictive power despite pairwise SCS correlating with NER confusion (Table~\ref{tab:pairwise}).
